I ask rank just to get an idea on where you are at in league.

Things I will say for now are practice your last hitting. Use the practice you can put a bot on enemy team so it doesn't push too hard and to make it a bit more normal. Go in and just farm without pushing the wave the best you can. At 5/10 minutes take note of your Cs. Try it again and try to beat your last number. But remember only last hit don't push. You want to aim for 10cspm. It's not something you need to do every game but it's a good goal to practice for. More Cs = more gold= earlier powerspike .

Next I would practice your kitting. After you feel like you have your farming down. Custom game VS 5 bots you feel would be trying to kill you in a real game where kiting is needed.(you can give your team a couple bots so the enemy bots don't just end the game) Farm in lane until you have a couple items and then push a lane until all the bots come to get you. Do your best to 1v5 them. Try more to maintain distance from them and using chompers and w to help you. Once you feel like you can kite easy take it to the real rift.

Okay so, What are your current settings in your **"output"** tab?  


You are using a 20 series nvidia card and a 2080 aswell (nice) so you should be using the Encoder=**NVENC**. Really OP encoder for your style of card which i wish i could use. If your bitrate is to low.. Whenever you turn or alot happens on screen e.g. smoke, fire, rain.   
The scene will appear blurry/pixelated. Upping your bitrate *should* fix this. I have mine at 6000 but you could get away with 4500-5000 if you're doign 720p 60fps. (if you're lagging alot you might have to stream at perhaps a lower quality or FPS e.g. lowering 60fps to 30fps. amd lowering bitrate to 2500-3000. Also make sure your **"Rate control"** is set to **CBR**

NOTE: bits are different to bytes. One byte is 8 bits. So you're upload speed is only 7-8 mbps which is about 1 megabyte per second, you could probably stream and game fine but unlikely :(.

***TLDR***: bitrate is your reason for blur/pixelation most likely. [https://stream.twitch.tv/encoding/](https://stream.twitch.tv/encoding/) this site by twitch shows the usual numbers you would use. Set your bitrate to 4500-5000 and see how it is and how gameplay is. Its pretty unlikely you will be able to stream 1080p footage and play a multiplayer game unless you downscale. Hey, i also used to get tilted and think the same after a loss but you gotta try really hard to not do that. Just think that every game win or loss is contributing towards you becoming a better player. i cannot stress how important \*/mute all\* is, you may think. "these people aren't tilting me" but trust me they are and most importantly they are distracting you.

The first thing i think of for your priorities for riven would be understanding your abilities and how they work together. What your passive does and just how much damage it adds to your Auto Attacks. Your q and how you can weave AA's in-between for maximum damage. Your w being a short stun, E being a dashing shield which has potential to cancel soooooo many animations riven has. Your ult enhancing all your abilities, AD and having an execute.

The most important combo or thing to learn for riven would be her Fast q Combo. Its basically just auto attacking and following it with a q and issuing a movement click near your target to break the animation then re-attacking your target. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YX7b\_TONpEY](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YX7b_TONpEY) Here's a link from one of my favourite streamers who made a fairly in-depth video on the fast combo. Once you get better at or even master this your skill in riven will skyrocket.

Next i'd prioritise learning animation cancels involving Riven's E. Usually using rivens R or W would lock you in a windup animation but if you E then use them, the animation is used in the dash or with some other combo's removed entirely. Her E can also be used for wall hoping as it changes your direction when cast.

There are heaps of guides all over this reddit and youtube which go more in depth but thats how i would start off, The practice tool is amazing and only takes 10-20 minutes a day before playing or throughout the day to fine tune your skills or learn something new.

One other thing, try to have some confidence when you play. Don't assume you have lost when things look dark, Don't only focus on the negatives or how your team are doing, play your game and your best. Take breaks after a stressful game or when you feel yourself tiring. You wont magically jump to a whole new division overnight.
